## 1. Current question, answer changed 2022 -> 2025

**Question:** Can a digital lender process borrower data on servers outside India?

### Naive (no version policy)

<!-- table: superseded_demo_table_2 -->
![Naive (no version policy)](data:image/png;base64,)

<!-- table: superseded_demo_table_3 -->
![Naive (no version policy)](data:image/png;base64,)

<!-- table: superseded_demo_table_4 -->
![Naive (no version policy)](data:image/png;base64,)

**Answer:** No.  A digital lender (NBFC or RE) must store all borrower data only in servers located within India.  If any data is processed outside India, it must be deleted from those external servers and the data brought back to India within 24 hours. Note: "Reserve Bank of India (Digital Lending) Directions, 2025" (issued 2025-05-08) has been withdrawn or superseded and replaced by "Reserve Bank of India (Non-Banking Financial Companies - Credit Facilities) Directions, 2025 (updated as on July 15, 2026)". The rule currently in force may differ.

### Versioned pipeline (default)

<!-- table: superseded_demo_table_5 -->
![Versioned pipeline (default)](data:image/png;base64,)

<!-- table: superseded_demo_table_6 -->
![Versioned pipeline (default)](data:image/png;base64,)

<!-- table: superseded_demo_table_7 -->
![Versioned pipeline (default)](data:image/png;base64,)

**Answer:** No.  An NBFC must store all customer data only on servers located within India.  If any processing occurs outside India, the data must be deleted from those overseas servers and brought back to Indian servers within 24 hours.

## 3. Current question, rule moved from the 2023 DLG guidelines into the 2025 Directions

**Question:** What is the cap on default loss guarantee in digital lending?

### Naive (no version policy)

<!-- table: superseded_demo_table_14 -->
![Naive (no version policy)](data:image/png;base64,)

<!-- table: superseded_demo_table_15 -->
![Naive (no version policy)](data:image/png;base64,)

<!-- table: superseded_demo_table_16 -->
![Naive (no version policy)](data:image/png;base64,)

**Answer:** The cap on a Default Loss Guarantee (DLG) cover is five percent of the total amount disbursed out of the loan portfolio at any given time. Note: "Reserve Bank of India (Digital Lending) Directions, 2025" (issued 2025-05-08) has been withdrawn or superseded and replaced by "Reserve Bank of India (Non-Banking Financial Companies - Credit Facilities) Directions, 2025 (updated as on July 15, 2026)". The rule currently in force may differ.

### Versioned pipeline (default)

<!-- table: superseded_demo_table_17 -->
![Versioned pipeline (default)](data:image/png;base64,)

<!-- table: superseded_demo_table_18 -->
![Versioned pipeline (default)](data:image/png;base64,)

<!-- table: superseded_demo_table_19 -->
![Versioned pipeline (default)](data:image/png;base64,)

**Answer:** The cap on default loss guarantee (DLG) is five percent (5%) of the total amount disbursed out of the loan portfolio at any given time.

## 4. Explicitly historical question (old text is allowed, must be labelled)

**Question:** How did the data storage requirement for digital lending change from the 2022 guidelines to the current rules?

### Naive (no version policy)

<!-- table: superseded_demo_table_20 -->
![Naive (no version policy)](data:image/png;base64,)

<!-- table: superseded_demo_table_21 -->
![Naive (no version policy)](data:image/png;base64,)

<!-- table: superseded_demo_table_22 -->
![Naive (no version policy)](data:image/png;base64,)

**Declined:** The current rules are not provided in the supplied sources. Only the superseded 2022 guidelines are available, so the change cannot be determined.

### Versioned pipeline (default)

<!-- table: superseded_demo_table_23 -->
![Versioned pipeline (default)](data:image/png;base64,)

<!-- table: superseded_demo_table_24 -->
![Versioned pipeline (default)](data:image/png;base64,)

<!-- table: superseded_demo_table_25 -->
![Versioned pipeline (default)](data:image/png;base64,)

**Answer:** The 2022 guidelines required that LSPs/DLAs store only basic minimal data, provide clear policy guidelines, prohibit biometric data, and store all data on servers within India. The current 2025‑2026 guidelines retain all these requirements but add that if any data is processed outside India, it must be deleted from the foreign servers and brought back to Indian servers within 24 hours of processing.

## 5. Superseded document whose successor is NOT in the corpus

**Question:** How often must banks carry out periodic KYC updation for high-risk customers?

### Naive (no version policy)

<!-- table: superseded_demo_table_26 -->
![Naive (no version policy)](data:image/png;base64,)

<!-- table: superseded_demo_table_27 -->
![Naive (no version policy)](data:image/png;base64,)

<!-- table: superseded_demo_table_28 -->
![Naive (no version policy)](data:image/png;base64,)

**Answer:** Banks must carry out periodic KYC updation for high‑risk customers at least once every two years. Note: "Master Direction - Know Your Customer (KYC) Direction, 2016" (issued 2016-02-25) has been withdrawn or superseded and replaced by entity-wise KYC Directions, 2025. The rule currently in force may differ.
